title: Cyclone Koji crosses north Queensland coast
detail: Tropical Cyclone Koji crossed between Ayr and Bowen; BOM recorded 362mm at Clarke Range in 24h and 370mm at Cattle Creek in 12h, with severe weather warnings Proserpine to Gladstone; about 22,000 homes lost power.
attribution: BOM, QFES and Ergon Energy via ABC

title: Ex-Cyclone Koji flood emergency at Clermont
detail: Isaac Regional Council issued a flood emergency warning for Clermont; major flood warnings for the Georgina, Connors-Isaac and Flinders rivers, with swift-water rescues in Clermont, Gracemere and Mackay.
agency: Isaac Regional Council / Bureau of Meteorology
attribution: Isaac Regional Council, QSES and BOM via ABC

title: Victorian bushfires destroy 228 homes
detail: Fires that began 7 Jan burnt about 404,000 ha, destroyed 228 homes (Longwood fire 142, Ravenswood South 54, Walwa 9) and more than 700 structures; one farmer died in the Longwood fire, per CFA and state authorities.
attribution: CFA and State Control Centre via ABC

title: Illicit tobacco factory raided in Rouse Hill
detail: The Illicit Tobacco Taskforce with ATO, TGA and NSW Police raided a Rouse Hill self-storage unit, seizing a cigarette machine the ATO said could make up to 3.6 million cigarettes a day, 7.5 kg of loose tobacco, about 6,000 vape components and counterfeit packaging.

title: Daly River town evacuated ahead of flood peak
detail: NT authorities declared an emergency evacuation of about 450 Daly River residents to Darwin as a tropical low dumped 300-500mm on the catchment; water and sewerage expected to be cut once the river passed 14 m.
agency: NT Police, Fire and Emergency Services
attribution: NT emergency authorities and BOM via AAP

title: Perth Invasion Day rally bomb declared terrorist act
detail: WA Police declared the attempted bombing of the Invasion Day rally in Perth's CBD a terrorist act and a 31-year-old man was charged with engaging in a terrorist act, WA's first such charge; police said the homemade fragment bomb with ball bearings and screws was racially motivated and failed to cause casualties.
attribution: WA Police Commissioner Col Blanch via ABC

title: OSB: three people-smuggling ventures resolved in February
detail: ABF's Operation Sovereign Borders update said three maritime people-smuggling ventures were resolved in February 2026 and 11 people returned to their country of departure (9 to country of origin); fewer than five were transferred to regional processing.
attribution: ABF/Joint Agency Task Force OSB monthly update

title: Chinese navy helicopter makes unsafe pass at RAN Seahawk
detail: Defence said a PLA-Navy helicopter closed to an unsafe distance and rolled toward an MH-60R from HMAS Toowoomba over the Yellow Sea during Operation Argos (UN sanctions monitoring on North Korea), forcing evasive action; no damage or injuries.
attribution: Australian Defence statement via USNI News

title: Katherine River hits 20-year high
detail: Katherine River peaked at 19.2 m at Katherine Bridge, highest in more than 20 years; about 500 people sheltered in evacuation centres, 208 evacuated from Daly River and all of Palumpa evacuated, per NT SES and NT government.
attribution: NTSES, BOM and NT Chief Minister via CityNews

title: Covert operation leads to 26 men charged with 1,000+ child abuse offences
detail: AFP said a Victoria JACET covert operation into encrypted sharing of violent child abuse material led to 26 men charged with more than 1,000 offences, plus 9 arrested by NSW Police on referral; about 65,000 unique files identified.

title: Cyclone Narelle upgraded to category 3
detail: BOM said Narelle was 780 km ENE of Cooktown with 165 km/h winds and could reach category 4 with gusts to 250 km/h before landfall between Lockhart River and Port Douglas; up to 450mm rain forecast.

title: Narelle makes landfall in three states
detail: BOM said Narelle hit Queensland as a category 4 (20 Mar), the NT as a category 3 (22 Mar) and WA's North West Cape as a severe category 4 (27 Mar), travelling about 6,500 km; only the second system on record to hit all three states as a severe cyclone.
place: Cape York Peninsula / Top End / North West Cape

title: Two Moree teens charged over extremist material
detail: NSW JCTT charged a 15- and a 16-year-old from Moree with violent extremist material offences; police alleged they seized handwritten extremist notes and a ballistic-style vest.

title: Nine charged over multi-tonne cocaine import conspiracy
detail: AFP said nine men aged 31-72 across Victoria, Sydney and Perth were charged in Operation Bruce Cremorne, a 10-month probe begun after a trawler sank off Port Albert, over alleged conspiracies to import tonnes of cocaine.
attribution: AFP media release (with Victoria Police, ABF, ACIC)

title: Cyclone Maila heads for Cape York
detail: BOM said Maila had weakened to category 2 and was expected to cross near Coen and Lockhart River the following week with gusts to 155 km/h; Queensland Health flagged melioidosis risk from heavy rain.

title: ABF apprehends two illegal fishing boats off Cape Wessel
detail: ABF officers from HMAS Cape Woolamai boarded and apprehended two foreign fishing vessels north of Cape Wessel, NT, finding evidence of fisheries offences; crews taken to Darwin.

title: Illegal fishing vessel seized in Torres Strait
detail: ABF patrol boat Storm Bay intercepted a suspected foreign fishing vessel near Mount Adolphus Island under Operation Broadstaff; ABF said it had intercepted 22 illegal foreign fishing vessels and seized over 6 tonnes of sea cucumber since 1 Jan 2026.

title: Canberra teen charged with planning terrorist act
detail: ACT Policing said a 17-year-old in custody since Nov 2025 was additionally charged with acts in preparation for a terrorist act, allegedly motivated by nationalist and racist views - the first such charge in the ACT.

title: AFP: 17 tonnes of drugs seized in Pacific in 2026
detail: AFP Commissioner Krissy Barrett told a Pacific Transnational Crime Summit in Suva that 17 t of illicit drugs, mostly cocaine, had been seized in early 2026 versus 4.6 t in all of 2025, calling Pacific trafficking a national security threat.

title: Darwin teen charged over nationalist extremist material
detail: AFP charged a 16-year-old in Darwin with possessing and distributing violent extremist material promoting nationalist ideology and possessing a prohibited weapon.

title: Clandestine drug lab found, six charged over AUD 39m cocaine
detail: AFP and ABF executed warrants at Kingsdale near Goulburn and in Sydney after 120 kg of cocaine was found in vehicle transmissions shipped from California; 44 kg cocaine and 2 kg meth found at an alleged lab. Six NSW men charged.

title: Record 2.7-tonne cocaine seizure (Operation Minjiang)
detail: AFP said 2.7 t of cocaine landed near Midge Point, Qld, was seized at a Londonderry property in western Sydney, bringing the operation to more than 3 t (street value about AUD 816 million); eight people charged.
attribution: AFP media release (with QPS, ABF, ACIC, AUSTRAC)

title: ASIO 2026 threat assessment keeps level at PROBABLE
detail: ASIO Director-General Mike Burgess kept the terrorism threat level at PROBABLE, warning of self-radicalising youths with blended nationalist, racist and anti-authority ideologies and alleging IRGC-linked actors were behind antisemitic attacks in Australia.
attribution: ASIO Director-General via Australian Security Magazine

title: Man fined AUD 31,000 over botched reptile smuggling
detail: A NSW man was fined AUD 31,000 for exporting fauna without authority after 65 reptiles taken near Narembeen and Merredin were posted from WA; parcels were intercepted at Perth and 55 of the animals died or were euthanised.
agency: WA Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions

title: 60 arrested in China-Australia tobacco smuggling takedown
detail: ABF and China Customs' Anti-Smuggling Bureau said Project Seahorse / Operation Trailblazer led to more than 60 arrests in China and seizure of over 60 million cigarettes in 91 containers bound for Sydney and other ports, with AUD 92 million in duty evaded.

title: Bondi antisemitism royal commission ends hearings
detail: The Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion, set up after the 14 Dec 2025 Bondi Hanukkah attack that killed 15, closed hearings after 346 witnesses and over 20,000 submissions; final report due 18 Dec 2026.
agency: Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion

title: Two new Evolved Cape patrol boats commissioned in Cairns
detail: Navy commissioned HMAS Cape Spencer and HMAS Cape Hawke at HMAS Cairns for border protection and maritime constabulary work, with range over 4,000 nm.
